units.translation: And these are the first causes of lamentations.
[after the words δυστόνων κακῶν ἄναξ διορθωτής [lord and corrector of grievous woes] M placed the words in the margin
Perhaps the leaders of this land would be watchers over us.
lord and corrector of grievous woes
For it is justice to honor the wife of a man who is the leader.
It is not found in the Attic writers, except in Aeschylus
but it is found in Herodotus and the Ionians. For examples from Pindar, Sophocles, and others see Thes. vol. 1, 2 p. 2114.

Thus Karsten for πομπούς τ᾿ ἀρχάς [escorts and leaders] (ἀρχούς [leaders] in some copies). A superlative formed from this noun (like βασιλεύτατος [most kingly] from βασιλεύς [king]) is perhaps to be restored at Ag. 255 τόδ᾽ ἄρχιστον Απίας γαίας μονόφρουρον ἕρκος [this chief sole-guardian bulwark of the Apian land], about which I have spoken in the Preface to the fifth Leipzig edition p. XC. Cf. ἀρχέστατος [most chief].
this chief sole-guardian bulwark of the Apian land
I begin, I begin for myself
The participle ἄρχων [ruling] is frequently used as a substantive meaning leader.

The active and middle forms differ in that the active refers to others who follow the ones beginning, the middle to those who themselves begin something and are going to finish it and the end of the matter: which distinction Galen best explains vol. 2 p. 7 (1 p. 13 Leipzig ed.)
like the verb δεσπόζειν [to be master] it is sometimes construed with the dative.
where ἅζονται [they are awed] is more probable, which Halm conjectured: see ἅζομαι [I am awed].
where, after removing the gloss, I corrected
And a Greek ship began the attack.
He began, O mistress, the whole evil, appearing as an avenger.
Zeus, Zeus, what shall I say, from where shall I begin?
As soon as the divinities began their wrath.
But I, he said, will begin with those of my own race, and my race will begin from me.
How far apart are ruling and being a slave.
He made peace for all his friends.
And the ruler of holy Memphis.
May he rule over the gods.
I will try to rule the citizens.
For he will not long rule over the gods,
Nor will they begin by falling to the ground,
Ruler against ruler and brother against brother, enemy with enemy I will stand.
And the impetuous ruler of many-men'd Asia.
Of such rulers I have now been reminded,
And there was no help for one another.
Left behind by that help, we remain.
Help for wars that avenge women.
